question: Who was the second Governor of Bombay (1669–1677) who is widely regarded as the 'founder' of the modern city of Bombay for his efforts in fortifying the town, establishing a mint, docks, and encouraging Indian traders to settle?
explanation: Gerald Aungier, who succeeded George Oxenden, was the Governor of Bombay from 1669 to 1677. He established the first mint, court of judicature, and constructed the fortifying walls, docks, and attracted merchants from Gujarat and Goa (Parsi, Bania, Hindu, Muslim) by offering religious tolerance.

question: Why did the English East India Company shift the headquarters of the Western Presidency from Surat to Bombay in 1687?
options: Surat was destroyed by a massive earthquake
Surat was constantly threatened by Maratha raids and Bombay offered an easily defensible, deep-water harbor
The Mughals expelled the English from Gujarat completely
explanation: Surat was vulnerable to land attacks and was sacked twice by Maratha ruler Chhatrapati Shivaji in 1664 and 1670. Bombay, being an island, possessed a superb natural harbor and was easier to defend using British naval superiority, prompting the EIC to shift the Western Presidency headquarters there in 1687.
